parking.calc: The ordinance ratios were not retrieved (all null), so this uses an ASSUMED medical office ratio of 1 per 200 SF (5/1000), to be verified. Building A 22,000 SF / 200 = 110; Building B 18,000 SF / 200 = 90. Total 200 stalls, about 70,000 SF with aisles. Buildings 40,000 SF + parking 70,000 SF + stormwater about 10,000 SF is about 120,000 SF (2.75 ac), inside the roughly 3.5 usable acres.

program.rationale: The Institutional future land use and the adjacent Wickshire Countryside assisted living community point to health and institutional uses. A two-building medical office campus on N McMullen Booth Rd suits that context and the Countryside demographics. The listing is only about 5 acres of a 12.9-acre parent parcel, so I sized the program to about 3.5 usable acres (5 ac less 30%) rather than the full 8.8 frontage-buildable acres. Zoning 'HF' could not be verified, so the use, the setbacks and the parking ratio all need a zoning verification letter.

zoning.notes: I could not find the ordinance for this district, so every dimensional and parking value is null rather than guessed. (1) A listing for the 3141 N McMullen Booth Rd parcel (parcel 21-28-16-00000-240-1100) says it is zoned 'HF' with an Institutional Future Land Use designation. It describes about 5 acres to be split from a larger parcel next to the Wickshire Countryside assisted living community. Your 12.909-acre figure may be the pre-split parent parcel, so check the lot's actual boundaries. (2) I found no 'HF' district in the City of Clearwater Community Development Code. Its institutional district is 'I' (Art. 2, Div. 12, sections 2-1201 to 2-1204). Other Clearwater districts that appeared in my results are the commercial, tourist, downtown and US 19 districts, none called HF. (3) 'HF' also did not appear in the unincorporated Pinellas County district list I could see (Chapter 138, Sec. 138-311, Municode). Unincorporated Pinellas County is therefore a possible administrator, but I could not confirm that either. 'HF' may be an abbreviation from the listing or a data vendor, or a district I did not retrieve. (4) Next steps: ask Clearwater Planning (Community Development) and Pinellas County Planning for a zoning verification letter, or check the parcel on the Pinellas County Property Appraiser and the Clearwater zoning atlas. Then pull the district's dimensional table, the off-street parking chapter, and the landscape and buffer rules. (5) Common Florida rules to check once the district is known: the buffer to residential, FDOT access spacing on N McMullen Booth Rd (a state or county arterial), and stormwater and impervious limits.
